rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding Y2O3 nanoparticles, while the target paper added 4.2 at.% Cr. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (oxide dispersion vs. alloying addition), so they do not match.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies high-temperature tensile and creep tests at 1100°C, whereas the target paper performed room-temperature compression tests. These are completely different testing regimes.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes Orowan strengthening from dispersed nanoparticles, while the target paper describes a dual mechanism of solid solution hardening and crack hindrance from a reticulated Laves phase. These are different mechanism classes.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts improved high-temperature strength and creep resistance, while the target paper reports concurrent increases in room-temperature yield strength and fracture strain. The properties and conditions differ entirely.
